title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with synthetic media, a real-time deepfake video call in which the caller presented himself as a sitting chief minister and actor. The failure sits at the point of contact between a citizen and a communication channel, a consumer messaging app, not inside any institution's own workflow. The system that was defeated was the victim's ability to tell a real public figure from a generated one, and the fraud then proceeded through ordinary payment requests and a second impersonation of a CBI officer.

Nothing in the call carried a check on the caller's identity. Catching it would have required confirming through a separate, trusted channel that the person on the video was who he appeared to be, or a platform-level means of flagging synthetic video in a live call. Neither existed here, and the requests for fees were the only signal available at the time.

What is not established is who produced the deepfake or operated the scheme, and the registered case is an allegation rather than a finding. The report is a single account from one complainant, and it does not show intent beyond the conduct described.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old Bengaluru security guard, Ratikanta Giri, from Odisha, lost more than Rs 1.04 lakh after a WhatsApp video call on Sept 9. The caller used an AI-generated deepfake to appear as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and actor C Joseph Vijay, offering Rs 11 lakh in aid. A supposed manager said Rs 5 lakh was allotted and asked for fees, including Rs 5,000, Rs 18,000, and over Rs 50,000. A person claiming to be a CBI officer also demanded money.

Giri made several payments through a digital payment app. When the fraudsters asked for another Rs 50,000, he refused and realized he had been duped. He contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then Byappanahalli police. A case has been registered under the Information Technology Act. Police urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on them. This was the first such case reported in the city.
